comment_data.body: `.pop()` isn't optional. But it has two variants that allow it to return arbitrary values (when given a default value). If we can't distinguish between the two variants here, then the return value must be `object`. (We might be able to distinguish the two programmatically elsewhere but probably not here.)

comment_data.body:
Unfortunatelly, no otherwise following code will break in the same way as reported in bug - e.g.:

```python
import cython

def main(d: dict[str,str]):
    v = d.pop('none')       # <------------ key found but still None returned, hence v needs to handle None value
    return len(v)

main({'none': None})
```
